messages:
Anna Ruiz: raising because Support got a customer complaint — p99 for text-gen API jumped to ~1.8s this morning for a production tenant. They sent example request ids and a sample prompt. Not seeing errors, just long tail latency. cc @Samir :alert:
Mia Chen: thanks — do we have metric slices? which model/route?
Anna Ruiz: customer is on hosted, model=redwood-1.2, route=/v1/generate. most of the high-p99 traces show batching wait times in the logs ("hold_ms") dominating. link to logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/abc123
Dan Patel: looking at the traces — majority show continuous-batcher waiting ~400ms before dispatch, even though request RT is small otherwise. We pushed a change to batcher last week that increased max_wait_ms default to 500ms for throughput experiments. probably related.
Samir Khan (oncall): ack. can we repro on staging with similar QPS? If it's config drift we should revert default quickly.
Anna Ruiz: Support provided an exact repro: a steady low-qps stream of small prompts (~30 tokens) from 1 client hitting a single instance. They said p50 is fine but p95/p99 spike periodically every 5-10min.
Mia Chen: that pattern screams microbatch fill + large timeout. Continuous batching tries to group requests to amortize GPU work, but with skewed arrival it can hold a request until either size or timeout triggers. If timeout is too high, tail suffers.
Dan Patel: immediate mitigation options:
- reduce continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 500 -> 50
- set continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens to 2048 -> lower to 512
- enable aggressive small-request fast-path (unbatched for < 64 tokens)
We can push a rollback to default in hosted config and canary to 5% traffic.
Samir Khan (oncall): do it. prefer config change not deploy. @ops-bot roll config: `PATCH /internal/configs/batcher` with payload below.
ops-bot: scheduled config patch for 5% canary in us-west-2. change: {"continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms":50, "continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens":512, "continuous_batcher.small_request_fastpath":true}
Mia Chen: repro steps I ran on staging (paste):
```
# simulate low qps single client
for i in {1..1000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"input":"short prompt","model":"redwood-1.2"}' &
  sleep 0.6
done
```
Observed p99 drop from ~1.6s -> 120ms after lowering max_wait_ms.
Dan Patel: logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-12T09:12:01Z] req=abc123 hold_ms=412 queued_tokens=8 dispatched_batch_tokens=1024
[2026-03-12T09:12:01Z] req=abc124 hold_ms=410 queued_tokens=6 dispatched_batch_tokens=1024
```
Anna Ruiz: Support updated customer that we're rolling a config change canary and will monitor; they asked for ETA. What's our rollout plan?
Samir Khan (oncall): roll to 5% canary now (ops-bot did). monitor p95/p99 and error rate for 20m. If stable, ramp 25% -> 100% over 30m. keep a rollback prepared to revert to 500ms if it causes throughput regressions.
Mia Chen: watch-outs: lowering max_wait_ms increases GPU kernel invocation frequency and may raise cost by ~6-12% for high-QPS customers. also watch batch size distribution (we'll add histogram metric: batch_size.percentiles).
Dan Patel: added a temporary metric alert: batcher.small_hold_ratio > 0.25 => paging SRE. also added a smoothing window on p99 to avoid noisy rollbacks.
ops-bot: canary status: deployed to 5% in us-west-2, config version v2026-03-12-17.
Samir Khan (oncall): monitoring — initial 10m looks good: canary p99 down to 140ms, no error spike. ramp to 25% now.
Anna Ruiz: customer confirmed improvement in their environment after the canary ramp. they reported p99 ~150ms on the sampled requests they shared. we'll keep them in the loop.
Mia Chen: follow-ups:
- make small_request_fastpath permanent behind a feature flag for the model.
- write a short runbook for support: how to inspect hold_ms in traces, suggested config knobs and cost tradeoffs.
- consider adaptive timeout based on per-route arrival patterns (experiment idea).
Dan Patel: creating a PR to add default small fastpath for redwood-1.x with opt-out. also documenting how to safely decrease max_wait_ms for Dedicated customers.
Samir Khan (oncall): good work. summarize for postmortem later if needed but this looks like config tuning, not a runtime bug. tagging postmortem=false for now. :thumbsup:
Anna Ruiz: thanks everyone. I'll close the ticket once customer confirms stability for 24h.
